correctness.rationale: The filled-hub equation eliminates b for eigenvalues below q. On the full leaf cube the eliminated operator is H_leaf−μI+(μ−λ)P_star, with μ=λ(1−λ)/(q−λ). For 0<λ<λ* the second eigenvalue is positive by min–max and the constant Rayleigh quotient is negative, so the operator cannot have a kernel. At λ* the pairing with the centered sum of leaf occupations forces g(star)=0, because the evaluation of the sum is nq and its product weight is p^n. The degree-one leaf spectrum then gives precisely the n−1 sum-zero contrasts; reconstruction is one-to-one and leaf averaging vanishes. The three-state n=1 chain has eigenvalues 0,q,2−q. Eighteen independently assembled symmetric matrices (n=1 through 6, q=0.16,0.5,0.84) agreed in first nonzero eigenvalue and multiplicity at tolerance 1e−10; the proof does not rely on them.
residual_risks: Finite diagonalizations are corroboration only. No statement for q endpoints, alternate clock normalization, or uniform symmetric-mode separation.

value.rationale: Identifying the whole gap space, rather than giving a single slow branch, determines which observables can decay at that rate. In particular every permutation-invariant observable misses all gap modes at finite n; this distinguishes radial relaxation from arbitrary relaxation without a total-variation claim.
residual_risks: No quantitative lower bound on the radial gap is claimed.
